header.title: Broadening capital cycle into machinery, software and manufacturing

s01_bottom_line.text: Today roughly four-fifths of spending in Canada's major capital-building sectors goes to structures and engineering rather than machinery and equipment; the next leg requires investment to broaden into machinery, software, IP and productive assets, with machinery-intensive investment, automation, processing and technology-intensive FDI in manufacturing and autos signaling the capital cycle is broadening.
Machinery-intensive investment, automation, processing and technology-intensive FDI would show that the capital cycle is broadening.

A shift toward machinery/equipment and technology-intensive investment would benefit Canadian manufacturing, automation and auto-related equities; the article quantifies neither the shift nor earnings effects and names no companies.
